hypotheses.justification: The statement stays true for N = ∅, so hN can be dropped. The proof would need extra work, and I have not written it out. Places are all non-trivial DVR valuation subrings of K containing k. The hypotheses force K to be a function field of trdeg 1 over the algebraically closed field k: `Algebra.EssFiniteType` makes K finitely generated, and Ω[K/k] of rank 1 forces trdeg = 1, because Ω[K/k] = 0 if K = k. For N = ∅, holRing ∅ is the intersection of all places, which is exactly k, the elements regular at every place. So the generator list n = 0, z = ![] works: the first conjunct is vacuous, and Algebra.adjoin k (range z) = ⊥ contains the image of k. Every f in the intersection is algebraic over k, hence lies in k because k is algebraically closed. The argument is as follows. If f were transcendental and in holRing ∅, then f ∈ holRing {Q} for any Q. The existing Dedekind-domain argument in `holRing_fg` shows holRing {Q} is the integral closure of k[f] in K, so it is Dedekind. Any maximal ideal (f − c) of k[f] lies under a maximal ideal of this integral closure. That gives a place where f − c is a non-unit and f has no pole anywhere. A place where t has a pole is also what `transcendental_of_not_mem` needs. So the nonempty hypothesis is only used to get `exists_fn` and a place Q₀ for transcendence, and an alternative argument covers the empty case. I am fairly but not fully certain, since the empty case needs a new proof.
